web.title: Meet the African startups that raised funding in July 2026
web.description:
# Meet the African startups that raised funding in July 2026
## ORA Technologies
Funding in July 2026: [$2 million Series A extension](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/moroccan-super-app-ora-technologies-raises-2-million-taking-series-a-funding-to-10-million/)

HQ: Morocco

Total funding since inception now sits at nearly $12 million. Azur Innovation Fund led the extension round alongside other Moroccan private investors.

## GrowForMe
Funding in July 2026: [Part of $500k from Village Capital](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/after-rivia-and-vdl-fulfilment-village-capital-invests-500k-in-three-more-ghanaian-startups/)

HQ: Ghana

Backed through Village Capital’s Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility.

## SAYeTECH
Funding in July 2026: [Part of $500k from Village Capital](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/after-rivia-and-vdl-fulfilment-village-capital-invests-500k-in-three-more-ghanaian-startups/)

HQ: Ghana

Co-founded by Theodore Ohene-Botchway, the company is preparing for wider market entry across the ECOWAS region.

## Reme-D
Funding in July 2026: [$1.45 million pre-Series A](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/after-500k-gif-backing-egypts-reme-d-raises-1-45-million-to-expand-molecular-diagnostics-manufacturing/)

HQ: Egypt

Founded in 2023 by Salma Tammam, Reme-D manufactures molecular diagnostic tests for diseases like tuberculosis, HIV, hepatitis, and HPV. The round was led by Anara Impact Capital, with participation from the Global Innovation Fund and Africa Health Ventures. It follows a $500k equity investment from the Global Innovation Fund in April.

## Orient Enterprises
HQ: Kenya

The company also runs its own tree nursery supplying seedlings to local farmers. Revenue hit $1.2 million in 2025, with more than 120 employees, 80% of them women. The investment came from climate investor Barka Fund.

## Mathesis Analytics
Funding in July 2026: Undisclosed

HQ: Nigeria

So far, it has helped provide over eight million loans to more than two million borrowers in Nigeria. The company received investment from First Ally Capital to expand its operations across Africa.

## Noma Services
Funding in July 2026: [$650k loan](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/nigerian-agribusiness-noma-services-secures-650k-working-capital-and-capex-loan/)

HQ: Abuja, Nigeria

## BrainsMingle
Funding in July 2026: [$400k Seed](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/brainsmingle-secures-400k-seed-investment-to-scale-its-video-first-professional-networking-platform/)

HQ: Egypt

The Seed round came from BasharSoft Group, Egypt’s largest human capital technology company, which runs WUZZUF and Forasna and serves over nine million users.

# Africa Health Ventures #31: Funding Is Back... Or Is It?
### 5-year-old ABA Life in Morocco secures $40 million to deliver AI for sovereign health
Just 36 companies had collectively raised less than $20 million in the first seven months of the year. The numbers were stark.

The funding winter may not be over, but there is still serious capital available to founders who build ambitious businesses, solve enterprise problems, and deliver long-term value to clients.

# Deals
- 🏥 **Medikea** in Tanzania [raised $1.2 million](https://disruptafrica.com/2026/10/26/tanzanian-e-health-startup-medikea-raises-1-2m-pre-seed-funding/) in pre-seed funding to grow its network of clinics, pharmacies and diagnostic labs alongside virtual consultations.
- 🏦 **[MyItura](https://myitura.com/)** in Nigeria secured seed investment from Africa Health Ventures to build the financial infrastructure for affordable healthcare across Africa. Their MediLoan product offers consumers healthcare credit to increase affordability for mass markets with and without insurance.
- 🌱 **[Tembelea](https://www.tembelea.health/)** secured pre-seed investment from Africa Health Ventures. Tembelea provides pharmacy as a service embedded inside Kenya’s primary care clinics — handling procurement, inventory, staffing, and software — so that the clinicians who run them can focus entirely on their patients.
- 🌍 **Madica** has [secured a $6 million commitment](https://www.wamda.com/2026/10/madica-secures-6-million-invest-30-african-startups) from Flourish Ventures to extend its pre-seed programme by three years. The money will back 25 to 30 more African startups and expand its company-building support.
- 💼 **Tanmiya Capital Fund II** in Egypt has [reached a final close of $130 million](https://www.avca.africa/news-insights/member-news/eib-commits-to-egypt-based-fund-manager/) to back established, high-growth Egyptian SMEs, including in healthcare.
